messages:
andrew: quick heads-up — after the kernel selector change landed in canary this morning we saw a series of OOMs on gtx-pool-3 and a ~25% tail-latency regression for long-context requests. attaching the profiler snippet and a few traces i grabbed.
andrew: profiler dump (abridged):
```
alloc failed: cudamalloc 0x1f4e0000 size=134217728
workspace usage: peak=5.2GB, reserved arenas=6.0GB, free fragments=1.8GB
kv-cache total_allocated=3.1GB, fragmentation_ratio=0.26
decode buffer spikes when seq_len>4096
latency p95 before=210ms after=265ms
```
andrew: root cause hypothesis: new kernel picks larger temporary buffers for fused attention on medium seqs which pushes total transient working set over allocator arena size -> fragmentation + per-request prefill for KV makes things worse.
michelle: thanks. that matches what i saw during local repro. fragmentation looks high because we didn't switch to the subarena allocator for the new kernels.
michelle: quick ideas:
- add a per-request KV prefill cap (e.g. cap prefill at 1.5M tokens total) so single big request can't prefill entire pool
- enable buffer reuse across decode <-> prefill paths (reuse decode buffers for prefill chunks)
- fall back to streaming decode kernel when reserved workspace < threshold
kai: ran a controlled canary with prefill cap=1.5M and workspace_reuse=true on three pods for 2h
- p95 dropped to 230ms
- peak memory reduced by ~900MB per pod
- no OOMs in that window
jordan: nice. two implementation notes:
1) evict policy: LRU by timestamp + prefer evicting low-use key prefixes (keys with < 2 hits in 10m)
2) when we evict, free in-place rather than returning to global allocator to reduce fragmentation churn
sara: for the allocator side: switching to 2-level arenas (global big arenas + per-stream mini-arenas) reduced fragmentation in my microbench by ~18%.
sara: command i used for profiling (cuda-memcheck + custom hooks):
```
./run_canary.sh --model redwood-v1 --seq 4600 --batch 2 --profiler=memtrack --duration=1800
# then: python tools/parse_memtrack.py out.json | jq '.peak, .fragments'
```
andrew: for rollout plan:
- short term (hotfix): set prefill cap=1.5M, enable workspace_reuse=true, revert kernel selector to prefer streaming when workspace free < 800MB
- medium term: implement 2-level arena allocator + in-place partial free on KV slab eviction
- tests: add fuzzing for large single-request prefill patterns and synthetic fragmentation scenarios
deploy-bot: deploy queued: rollback kernel-selector v2 -> v1 on canary (scheduled) 

michelle: i'll pick up the prefill cap + workspace_reuse flags. aim to deploy by EOD to canary and monitor.
kai: i’ll keep the canary running and share dashboards (latency, OOM count, fragmentation metric) at +30m intervals.
andrew: thanks team. if we still see OOMs after the hotfix we'll throttle prefill to decode-only (no prefill) for requests > 6k tokens as a failsafe. :thumbsup:
